parts:
Hi folks,

Forgive me if this is a basic question, as I am just becoming familiar with Wallace and species distribution models. I have moved on from present and future predictions of the distribution of my focal species using Wallace's default settings (19 Bioclim variables) to now providing Wallace some of my own rasters (soil and elevation data) in addition to the Bioclim data to make predictions about the present potential distribution of my focal species.

I'm also interested in projecting the distributions of my focal species into the future using the aforementioned variables. I have the rasters, but am not sure how to generate the model. How might I go about doing this, as the options for "future projection" are gone with user-specified environmental conditions? Thank you for your time and consideration!

Best,
Nolan Amon
Ph.D. Student, Department of Entomology
University of Wisconsin-Madison

messages.author: 881c0dd9c7b0d196
messages.subject: Re: Future projections with user-specified environmental variables
parts:
Hi Nolan, thanks for checking in.

Are you running v1? This is the version that is currently on CRAN. It offers the ability to upload your own user variables as environmental data but does not allow user uploads for projecting. It does have capabilities to transfer the model to a new time period using WorldClim future bioclim variables, but this only works if you built the model using WorldClim bioclimatic variables. The future variables need to correspond to the variables you built the model with, so if you uploaded your own variables instead of using WorldClim, the option will disappear.
I think this is what you meant by saying the options were gone, but v2 (which will be on CRAN very soon!) is stable and can be installed through GitHub. (Check out the vignette for install instructions & info on transferring to future environments). 

 In v2, the module “Transfer to User Environments” can be used to upload your own future rasters to transfer the model to. Please note: this version has updated the terminology from “project” to the more appropriate “transfer”, since project is commonly used in GIS for changing the map projection; "Project" in v2 is now "Transfer" in v2. To use this module, just make sure your future rasters are named similarly to your initial rasters. (there will be a message regarding proper naming in the window).

Let me know if this answered your question.

Bethany Johnson

I've seen both issues you brought up before, hopefully I can help you fix them.

For me, it happens after I download result data, so you can fix it by closing out the download panel bar at the bottom. You can also try resizing the browser window, sometimes this helps the map reset. Whatever you do, don't refresh the page- you'll lose your work!

Bethany

messages.subject: Re: Future projections with user-specified environmental variables
parts:
I'll take a look into the biomod2 issue.

As for the projection problem, it is probably due in an error importing the future data. The future variables need to be uploaded in the exact order as your original variables. So for example, if you used: bio01, bio02, bio03, and then soil, then the future variables will need to be future bio01, future bio02, future bio03, future soil... You can check back to see what you've uploaded in the window log (I think there will also be a pop up message above the upload option). Be careful using drag & drop, sometimes this will put them in the wrong order (e.g., 3, 2, 1 instead of 1,2,3).
Hope that helps!

Bethany
